t.E306.agn: In 2015 EFSA found no safety concern at the use levels as a food additive; it could not set a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) because data on reproduction and development were insufficient. The upper intake level of vitamin E for adults is 300 mg a day.
t.E306.body: The fate of tocopherols in the body is not fully known. In rats, 3–15% of the amount taken by mouth, and up to 25% at high doses, is excreted in the faeces; almost no tocopherol is excreted unchanged in the urine, though some breakdown products are. Amounts in excess of requirements are partly stored in the liver.
t.E306.prod: Obtained by vacuum steam distillation of vegetable oils.
t.E306.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no safety concern at the use levels, no ADI could be set (insufficient data).
t.E306.summary: An antioxidant from the vitamin E family. It is obtained from vegetable oils or synthesised and delays the spoilage of fats.
t.E306.what: A tocopherol-rich extract; it delays fats oxidising and going rancid. Tocopherols belong to the vitamin E family and are also taken in naturally with food.
